newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices slide over weak swaps.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Prices slide over weak swaps.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market edged lower on Thursday despite anticipation from some suppliers that prices might hold over a drop in Singapore's weekly residue stocks, traders said.
In line with weak swaps and crude values, suppliers brought down their offers to $100.50 per tonne from earlier $102-$103.5.
A trader sold 20,000 tonnes of 180-cst grade at $101.5 for delivery March 21-25.
March swaps fell to $98.00/$99.00 per tonne and April dropped to $95.50/$96.25 from Wednesday's $99.50/$100.50 and $97.75/$98.50 respectively.
Despite several bids and offers, overall market sentiment remained cautious, with traders searching for a clear trend to follow.
Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) announced on Thursday the residue fuel oil stocks fell by 1.634 million barrels to 10.595 million barrels in the week ending March 5.
Some suppliers were optimistic about the drop but some differed in opinions.
"I don't think we can be too happy about it. The stocks just came back to the normal level," said one trader, comparing with the hike a week earlier.
Stocks reached a nine-month high to over 12 million barrels last week.
However, several scheduled maintenance turnarounds in Singapore later in March were expected to support sentiment.
"The turnarounds should be able to digest some stocks before Chinese buyers re-enter the market," the trader said.
Chinese buyers have been seen making enquiries for April cargoes and some traders expected Chinese activities to emerge soon after being absent from the market for nearly two months.
LSWR eased in the absence of demand in the thin market, traders said.
